prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the near camera-wearer’s hands and counter edge (roughly 0.2–0.7 m) from the standing person across the counter (about 0.8–1.8 m) and the darker rear kitchen surfaces (roughly 2–4 m); the sink and worktop run across the foreground, with the person generally ahead and shifting from left to center-right as the camera turns right. Across frames, the person becomes larger and brighter, indicating approach or decreasing camera-to-person distance, while the bowl, cutting board, beans, appliances, and orange remain clustered on the counter within about 0.5–1.5 m of that person and mostly within about 0.5–2 m of the camera wearer. The person is side-on and looking downward toward the work surface rather than clearly toward the camera, but depth alone does not resolve gaze or facing direction reliably. Bright silhouettes make near surfaces and occlusions—especially the person blocking the counter behind them—clearer than RGB alone, although the person’s shirt and nearby surfaces saturate together, object boundaries are smeared, and metric distances are only rough monocular estimates.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates one person in every frame and intermittently identifies two bowls, a bottle, a donut-shaped item, and an orange, making their left-right ordering and persistence clearer than in RGB: the person moves from left of center toward the center/right, bowls remain on the counter near the person, and the orange stays farther right. The person is approximately 0.8–2 m from the camera wearer, while the labeled counter objects are roughly 0.5–1.8 m away and generally within about 0.2–0.8 m of the person; these distances come mainly from RGB scale because segmentation itself provides no depth. The masks show partial occlusion and cropping well—the person is repeatedly cut off by frame boundaries, their torso/arm hides nearby counter regions, and several small objects appear only in some frames—but they do not reliably show front-versus-behind, gaze, or arm’s reach without added geometry. Reliability is limited because many visible structures and objects are unlabeled, the person’s mask changes color and shape, one bowl/donut detection is inconsistent, and the bottle and orange appear only intermittently despite remaining in the scene.
descriptions.pose: The pose map emphasizes articulated geometry: a single person’s body shifts from upright at the left to a larger, partly cropped torso near the center/right, while magenta hand keypoints appear near the counter in later frames and the camera wearer’s or another near hand/arm is partly visible at the edges. The skeleton suggests the person faces mostly sideways toward the counter with arms extended downward or forward; their hands are roughly 0.2–0.6 m from the bowl/work surface and therefore within their arm’s reach, while nearby magenta hand detections appear roughly 0.3–0.8 m from the camera wearer. Across the five frames, the body grows and moves rightward, consistent with decreasing separation or a rightward camera turn, and limb orientation changes from mostly vertical to more horizontal as occlusion and cropping increase. Compared with RGB, the map makes joint and hand locations easier to separate from clutter, but it is unreliable for precise distance, gaze, and full-body orientation because many joints are missing, several limbs are connected implausibly, hands are fragmented, and the lower body is largely outside the view.
